note: The research record published on the site. Every number is copied verbatim from CLAUDE.md; where CLAUDE.md records no interval, the interval is null. verdict: retired (tested, no edge) | null (tested, no effect) | not_testable (data does not exist) | open (awaiting a holdout).

hypotheses.question: Do sportsbooks overprice longshot player props?
hypotheses.metric: realized rate in the 0.125-0.150 price bucket (priced 0.1388)
hypotheses.why: Every settled observation priced below 0.15 is a sacks over on a single-book 1-2 line ladder, and even there the priced value sits inside the Wilson interval.

hypotheses.question: Does the model's week-1 entry beat the Kalshi close?
hypotheses.why: Mid-to-mid CLV was +0.62pp [+0.13, +1.22], but the book tightened from below; where money changes hands CLV is deeply negative.

hypotheses.question: Held to settlement, does one crossing at the touch pay?
hypotheses.metric: one-crossing CLV against the closing mid
hypotheses.why: Exactly mid-to-mid minus half the 7.22c entry spread; shrinking the ticket buys back slippage and nothing else.

hypotheses.question: Would a resting maker order on the model's side have earned the spread?
hypotheses.metric: maker CLV conditional on a fill
hypotheses.why: Fill rate 18.0%; the fills were worth nothing while the misses were worth everything (selection gap +4.52pp [+3.58, +5.79]).

hypotheses.question: Does the model's side selection add value over a model-free maker control?
hypotheses.metric: conditional maker CLV, model's own side, 100 contracts
hypotheses.why: The flipped side reads +0.07pp [-0.69, +0.93]; the weekly product peaks at ~$113/week at 250 contracts - real but small.

hypotheses.question: Do Kalshi ladder rungs violate monotonicity on the touch, tradeably?
hypotheses.metric: violation episodes surviving taker fees on both legs
hypotheses.why: 95% are in-game rungs updating out of step; where depth could be checked the thinner leg carried a median of 1 contract, max 2.

hypotheses.question: Do first-TD-scorer partitions sum to more or less than 1?
hypotheses.why: 13 of 16 settled week-1 events had no No Touchdown leg, so the partition sum is undefined.

hypotheses.question: Does quoting both sides capture the spread, per series?
hypotheses.why: Negative on every tight series and zero on the prop series; spread and maker fee are collinear, so the ordering cannot separate them.

hypotheses.question: Does Kalshi's team-market price lag the sportsbook consensus by more than it costs to cross?
hypotheses.metric: mean gap, Kalshi mid minus de-vigged consensus
hypotheses.why: Pre-kickoff gaps above 2.5pp were three claims on minority half-point lines and CLV to Kalshi's own close was -0.9pp; in-game gaps were book clock skew.

hypotheses.question: Is the model's probability better than the market's on settled outcomes?
hypotheses.why: Worse than the market, with the interval excluding zero and the estimate above the minimum detectable effect. Restated 2026-09-17 after the settlement fix: the population grew from 682 to 706 as played-with-no-stat-row outcomes began settling at 0, and the model now scores IDENTICALLY to the smoothed prior-season rate (0.1916 against 0.1916) rather than merely close to it.

hypotheses.question: After a player reaches a receptions rung mid-game, is the winning side still offered?
hypotheses.metric: executable net per contract at 120s, 10 contracts, depth-confirmed
hypotheses.why: Passes four of five bars and awaits week-2 replication; about $17 for the week, and final-stat determination is look-ahead against the live feed.

hypotheses.question: Does order-book imbalance predict a move larger than the spread plus fee?
hypotheses.metric: top-decile move minus half-spread and fee
hypotheses.why: The in-game slope is real and replicates on college football, but net of cost is negative in all 30 NFL and all 16 estimable CFB cells; the largest gross move is ~1.1pp against 1.5-24pp of cost.

hypotheses.question: When is the Kalshi book widest and tightest?
hypotheses.metric: spread lifecycle (execution map, not an edge)
hypotheses.why: Cross game lines 1-6h before kickoff; never cross a prop in-game, where REC spreads reach 16c and RSHATT 63c on 1-2 contracts.

hypotheses.question: Does an open scan of week 1 find anything that clears five pre-registered bars?
hypotheses.why: 396 search tests, 230 at nominal p<0.05 against 16.4 expected; the replicating effects all lose to cost.

hypotheses.question: Walk-forward, does the model beat the de-vigged sportsbook close?
hypotheses.why: Worse in every season (2023 +0.0229, 2024 +0.0237) against an MDE of ~0.008, and in all 13 variants bracketing the model's unverified constants. Restated 2026-09-17 after the settlement fix, which grew every season's sample and collapsed the separate corrected arm into the primary one - it now reports 0 outcomes moved.

hypotheses.question: Do sportsbooks disagree enough for arbitrage or middles?
hypotheses.why: Arbs appear on 2.53% of receptions opportunities from slow books, fail replication, and are worth ~$5 per $500 instance before limiting; every middle loses.

hypotheses.question: Do teammates' lines lag an inactive announcement?
hypotheses.metric: inactive events with an announcement timestamp
hypotheses.why: No source on disk timestamps an inactive; Kalshi pulled a Friday-OUT player's markets on Saturday, removing the game-day window for known outs.
